# FDG5127

> DO prefer descriptive types over tuples, `System.Tuple<T1, ...>`, and `System.ValueTuple<T1, ...>`; they improve discoverability and can better evolve over time.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.9 Using Tuples in Member Signatures.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Library only: the Toub annotation says that the tuple guidelines are about public APIs, and that tuples are handy in implementation. Analyzer candidate rejected: the body of FDG5128 allows a named tuple for a method so specialized that its result would never be amended and would only be deconstructed, which is intent. FDG5128, FDG5130, FDG5131 and FDG5132 report the mechanical cases.

## From the book

> **Stephen Toub:** Neither discoverability nor evolution is particularly important for internals. It’s good to remember that the guidelines here are about public APIs. Tuples (and the syntax C# provides for them) are really handy in implementation and are a convenient way of passing around multiple pieces of related data, including when providing multiple return values from methods.
